chunks: His command is only when He wills a thing that He says to it: "Be," and it is.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Kun' in Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ya-Sin 36:82) is often cited to affirm God's absolute sovereignty and the simplicity of His creative command, contrasting with the complexity of created beings. It underscores the concept of 'Kun Fayakun' as a direct manifestation of divine will, reinforcing the belief in God's power to create from nothingness without intermediary causes. This principle is frequently used in theological discussions to highlight the immediacy of God's decree and the ease with which He brings about any desired outcome.
